audit_metadata.title: Statistical Inference and Reporting Correction Addendum
audit_metadata.benchmark: NASA C-MAPSS FD004 Official Test Set (N=248 Engines)

families_defined.description: 5 pairwise model contrasts evaluated separately for MAE, RMSE, and NASA score
Pre-specified comparisons of proposed FailureDNA (Regime-Aware) against 3 established baselines (XGBoost, Random Forest, Linear Ridge)
All 15 hypothesis tests across all 5 pairwise model contrasts and all 3 metrics

key_findings.interpretation: XGBoost advantage in MAE remains statistically significant across all multiple-comparison family corrections (adjusted p <= 0.015).
Nominally significant at alpha=0.05 (p=0.0270), but loses statistical significance once adjusted for multiple comparisons (adjusted p=0.1080).

key_findings.comparison: FailureDNA (Regime-Aware) vs Random Forest in MAE
key_findings.interpretation: Nominally significant (p=0.0340), but not statistically significant after Holm correction in any family (adjusted p >= 0.0680).

key_findings.comparison: All RMSE and NASA Score Comparisons
key_findings.interpretation: All 95% bootstrap confidence intervals include zero. No model demonstrates statistically verifiable superiority on RMSE or NASA score.

nasa_score_uncertainty_analysis.instability_mechanism: The NASA metric's exponential penalty creates heavy-tailed, highly skewed per-engine score contributions. A single engine error swing of 30 cycles changes the penalty by hundreds of points. In bootstrap resampling, the presence or absence of top outlier engines (Unit 54: -908 pts, Unit 153: +852 pts) causes the total fleet score difference to swing between -3,760 and +3,088 points. The confidence interval includes zero, confirming that point-estimate rankings on NASA score cannot support claims of statistical superiority.

reporting_distinctions.point_estimate_ranking: FailureDNA (Regime-Conditioned) ranks 1st in NASA score (7,691), FailureDNA (Regime-Aware) ranks 2nd (8,049), XGBoost ranks 3rd (8,186). On MAE and RMSE, XGBoost ranks 1st (20.56, 29.08).
reporting_distinctions.nominal_statistical_evidence: Nominal unadjusted tests show p < 0.05 for XGBoost vs FailureDNA in MAE (p=0.0010 and p=0.0270) and RF vs FailureDNA in MAE (p=0.0340).
reporting_distinctions.multiplicity_adjusted_evidence: After Holm-Bonferroni correction, only XGBoost's MAE superiority over FailureDNA (Regime-Aware) is statistically verified (adjusted p=0.0050). No other contrast is statistically significant.
reporting_distinctions.uncertainty_and_limitations: Wide paired confidence intervals in NASA score (spanning zero) reflect heavy-tailed metric instability rather than definitive parity or superiority.
